title: Marine Diesel Engines
description: Test your knowledge of marine diesel engine operation, fuel injection, lubrication, cooling, combustion, fault diagnosis and safety.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a marine diesel engine?
options: To store ballast water
To cool the cargo holds
To propel the vessel or generate electrical power
To clean the exhaust gas
questions.explanation: Marine diesel engines are mainly used for propulsion or for driving generators that produce electrical power.

questions.question: Which fuel is commonly used in large marine diesel engines?
options: Heavy fuel oil or marine diesel oil
Aviation gasoline
Fresh water
Hydraulic oil
questions.explanation: Large marine engines commonly operate on heavy fuel oil, marine diesel oil or other approved marine fuels.

questions.question: What happens inside the cylinder during combustion?
options: Cooling water pushes the piston downward
Lubricating oil is converted into fuel
Exhaust gas is stored in the cylinder
Fuel burns and produces expanding gases that push the piston
questions.explanation: The injected fuel ignites in the hot compressed air, creating high-pressure gases that force the piston downward.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the fuel injection system?
options: To pump seawater through the engine
To deliver the correct quantity of fuel at the correct time
To remove lubricating oil
To control the rudder
questions.explanation: The injection system meters, pressurizes and injects fuel into the cylinder at the correct point in the engine cycle.

questions.question: Why is lubricating oil used in a marine diesel engine?
options: To increase exhaust temperature
To reduce friction and wear between moving components
To replace the cooling water
To increase the vessel's draft
questions.explanation: Lubricating oil reduces friction, limits wear, removes some heat and helps protect engine components from corrosion.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the engine cooling system?
options: To remove excess heat and maintain safe operating temperatures
To increase fuel viscosity
To raise exhaust pressure
To reduce propeller diameter
questions.explanation: The cooling system transfers heat away from components such as cylinder liners, cylinder heads and pistons.

questions.question: In a four-stroke diesel engine, how many crankshaft revolutions are required to complete one operating cycle?
options: One revolution
Three revolutions
Four revolutions
Two revolutions
questions.explanation: A four-stroke cycle consists of intake, compression, power and exhaust strokes and requires two crankshaft revolutions.

questions.question: What is the main difference between a two-stroke and a four-stroke marine diesel engine?
options: A two-stroke engine completes a cycle in one crankshaft revolution
A two-stroke engine does not require fuel
A four-stroke engine has no exhaust system
A four-stroke engine cannot drive a generator
questions.explanation: A two-stroke engine completes one full operating cycle during one crankshaft revolution, while a four-stroke engine requires two.

questions.question: What is scavenging in a two-stroke marine diesel engine?
options: Cleaning fuel tanks with seawater
Filtering lubricating oil
Removing exhaust gases and supplying fresh air to the cylinder
Heating the cylinder liner
questions.explanation: Scavenging replaces exhaust gases in the cylinder with fresh pressurized air before the next combustion cycle.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a turbocharger on a marine diesel engine?
options: To cool the lubricating oil
To use exhaust energy to compress more intake air into the engine
To operate the ballast pumps
To reduce the crankshaft speed to zero
questions.explanation: The turbocharger uses exhaust-gas energy to drive a compressor, increasing the mass of air supplied to the cylinders.

questions.question: Why must heavy fuel oil normally be heated before injection?
options: To increase its water content
To prevent compression in the cylinder
To reduce the amount of intake air
To reduce its viscosity and improve atomization
questions.explanation: Heavy fuel oil is heated so that it reaches the correct viscosity for pumping, injection and fine atomization.

questions.question: What may happen if a fuel injector does not atomize the fuel correctly?
options: Poor combustion, increased smoke and carbon deposits
Improved fuel efficiency
Lower cylinder pressure with perfect combustion
The cooling system stops using water
questions.explanation: Poor atomization produces larger fuel droplets, resulting in incomplete combustion, smoke, deposits and reduced efficiency.

questions.question: One cylinder has a significantly higher exhaust-gas temperature than the other cylinders at the same engine load. What is the most likely interpretation?
options: The cylinder may have poor combustion, incorrect fuel injection or reduced air supply
The cylinder is producing no power and receives no fuel
The crankshaft speed is too low only at that cylinder
The lubricating-oil sump contains too much water
questions.explanation: A high exhaust temperature on one cylinder can indicate over-fuelling, poor atomization, late injection, leaking exhaust valves or insufficient combustion air.

questions.question: During starting, the main engine turns slowly on starting air but does not reach firing speed. Which condition is a plausible cause?
options: Insufficient starting-air pressure or excessive mechanical resistance
Excessive fuel atomization
A fully open exhaust-gas bypass
Low seawater salinity
questions.explanation: Low starting-air pressure, restricted air flow, leaking starting valves or excessive engine resistance can prevent the engine from reaching the required firing speed.

questions.question: An oil-mist detector alarm is activated in the crankcase. What should be the primary concern?
options: The possible development of a hot spot and crankcase explosion risk
A reduction in ballast-tank pressure
An increase in exhaust-gas cleaning efficiency
A malfunction in the freshwater generator
questions.explanation: Oil mist can be produced when lubricating oil contacts an overheated bearing or other hot surface, creating a risk of crankcase explosion.

questions.question: Why should crankcase doors not be opened immediately after a suspected crankcase fire or oil-mist alarm?
options: Fresh air entering the crankcase could create an explosive mixture or cause re-ignition
The crankshaft may immediately rotate in reverse
Cooling water may enter the fuel system
The turbocharger may lose lubrication
questions.explanation: Opening the crankcase too early may introduce oxygen into a hot oil-mist atmosphere, increasing the risk of fire or explosion.

questions.question: A scavenge-space fire is suspected in a slow-speed two-stroke engine. Which observation would support this diagnosis?
options: Rising scavenge temperature, smoke and sparks near the affected cylinder
Low fresh-water tank level with normal exhaust temperature
Stable scavenge temperature and reduced fuel viscosity
Increased starting-air receiver pressure
questions.explanation: A scavenge fire may produce high local temperatures, smoke, sparks, unstable engine operation and elevated exhaust temperatures.

questions.question: A main bearing temperature rises rapidly while lubricating-oil pressure remains normal. What is the most appropriate interpretation?
options: Local bearing damage or loss of effective lubrication may still be developing
Normal oil pressure proves that the bearing cannot be damaged
The fuel injector is supplying too little fuel
The starting-air distributor is incorrectly timed
questions.explanation: Normal system pressure does not guarantee that every bearing receives adequate lubrication. Local blockage, misalignment or bearing damage can still cause overheating.

questions.question: Turbocharger fouling causes a reduction in compressor efficiency. What is the most likely effect on engine operation?
options: Reduced air supply, poorer combustion and higher exhaust temperatures
Increased air supply and lower cylinder pressure
Lower fuel consumption with no change in combustion
Higher cooling-water pressure and improved scavenging
questions.explanation: A fouled turbocharger supplies less air for combustion, which can cause smoke, increased exhaust temperatures and reduced engine efficiency.

questions.question: Why must cylinder-oil feed rate be adjusted carefully on a low-speed two-stroke engine?
options: Too little oil increases liner wear, while too much oil can increase deposits and operating cost
Cylinder oil controls starting-air pressure
Cylinder oil determines the engine's cooling-water temperature
Excess cylinder oil increases propeller pitch
questions.explanation: Insufficient cylinder lubrication can cause corrosive and adhesive wear, while excessive lubrication may create deposits and waste oil.

questions.question: Cylinder-pressure measurements show that one cylinder has lower peak pressure than the others, while compression pressure is approximately normal. Which fault is most plausible?
options: Incorrect fuel injection quantity or timing in that cylinder
Severe leakage past the piston rings during compression
A blocked cooling-water outlet from the cylinder head
Excessive starting-air pressure
questions.explanation: Normal compression with reduced peak pressure often points to a combustion or fuel-injection problem rather than major compression leakage.
